title: No role definition declares a provider, a model or a thinking level
summary: No shipped role definition declares a provider, a model or a thinking level, and the role-definition check fails one that does (TSK-0051, against ACC-0073). SCOPE. This is a STATIC check of what the three shipped definitions declare. No specialist process was launched and none is claimed: what a real child actually receives - its active tool set, and its inherited provider, model and thinking level - is ACC-0076's measurement under TSK-0053, which owns the delegation runtime. STRUCTURAL, NOT A BLOCKLIST. The rendered frontmatter has a closed key set - name, role, description, tools, in that order and nothing else - so a `model:` line is not a field somebody forgot to reject: it is a key outside the set, and the reader refuses it as one. The authored data is closed the same way, at seven prose fields, so no role can author a model either. TEN NAMED REFUSALS. provider, model, models, thinking, thinkingLevel, reasoning, reasoningEffort, apiKey, baseUrl and api are each refused under `frontmatter-declares-model-selection` rather than as an unknown key, because a criterion that names model selection deserves a refusal that names it back, and because "you may not choose a model here" is a better sentence for an operator than "unknown key". A mutation narrowing that list to `model` alone is killed. THE SHIPPED FILES. All three are asserted to contain no provider, model, thinkingLevel, thinking, reasoning, apiKey or baseUrl line, and separately to carry no credential, no drive-lettered path, no home directory and no model name such as gpt- or claude-. WHY IT MATTERS, from CMP-0035's own note: a role-shipped model would silently override the operator's project selection, which REQ-0025 requires to be chosen by the operator from what discovery reports and recorded as reproducible project configuration.
